verdict.summary: Register a Server-based client in the Zoho API Console and any Zoho CRM user can authorize it the same day; the docs we read describe no app review or verification step. The real work is engineering: routing each user to their data center, staying under per-org API credits, and the 20-refresh-tokens-per-user cap.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Register a Server-based client, run the code flow with access_type=offline, call the API.

timeToProd.assumes: A Server-based client with Multi-DC enabled and ZohoCRM.modules scopes, distributed from your own site; a Zoho Marketplace listing is a separate, optional path.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: None of the OAuth, registration, scopes or multi-DC pages mention a review. Absence of a documented review is not proof that none exists.

prerequisites.item: A Zoho account with access to Zoho CRM (a free or trial org works for testing)
prerequisites.why: You sign in to the API Console with a Zoho account, and users pick the CRM organization when they grant access.

prerequisites.item: A backend with an HTTPS redirect URI
prerequisites.why: Server-based clients need a backend and web UI to handle the redirect; the redirect_uri must match the registered one.

prerequisites.item: Customers on a paid edition for real agent workloads
prerequisites.why: The Free edition gets 5,000 API credits a day and a concurrency limit of 5, which a busy agent can exhaust quickly.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Limits are sourced; that they are too low for agents is our inference.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: scopes_supported in accounts.zoho.com's OIDC discovery document.

scopeTiers.impact: Read records and query with COQL. Access is still limited by the user's CRM profile and role.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: No approval requirement is mentioned on the scopes page.

scopeTiers.impact: Create, update and delete records, run bulk jobs, and subscribe to change notifications.
Manage settings, users and org data. Works only as far as the authorizing user's own permissions allow.

steps.title: Sign in to the Zoho API Console
steps.detail: Sign in with a Zoho account and click Get Started.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The console URL returned HTTP 302 (to sign-in) on 2026-10-20. We did not sign in.

steps.title: Register a Server-based client
steps.detail: Choose Server-based Applications, enter client name (no special characters except _ and &), homepage URL and redirect URI, then Create. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the Client Secret tab.

steps.title: Enable Multi-DC
steps.detail: On the client's Settings tab, turn on Multi DC and pick which data centers' users can connect. Client ID stays the same; secrets can differ per DC.

steps.title: Pick least-privilege scopes
steps.detail: Use service.scope.operation scopes, e.g. ZohoCRM.modules.READ,ZohoCRM.coql.READ for read-only agents; add CREATE/UPDATE or ALL only where needed.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Send users to https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/auth with response_type=code, client_id, scope, redirect_uri and access_type=offline. Read location and accounts-server from the callback, then exchange the code (valid 3 minutes) at {accounts-server}/oauth/v2/token.

steps.title: Route API calls per data center
steps.detail: Store location, accounts-server and the API domain per connection. Call the matching zohoapis host (e.g. www.zohoapis.eu) and refresh against the same accounts server.

steps.title: Implement token caching and refresh
steps.detail: Cache the 1-hour access token and reuse it; at most 10 access tokens per refresh token per 10 minutes. Avoid re-running consent repeatedly, since each user keeps at most 20 refresh tokens and the oldest is invalidated.

steps.title: Budget API credits and concurrency
steps.detail: Track per-org daily credits (Free 5,000; paid editions 50,000 plus per-user credits) and concurrency (5–25 per org per app). Use notifications and bulk APIs instead of tight polling.

steps.title: Test with users from more than one data center
steps.detail: Connect a US account and at least one non-US account (e.g. EU or IN) to confirm DC routing works end to end.

agentCanDo: Implement the code flow with access_type=offline and DC-aware token exchange
Build per-connection routing for accounts and API domains
Implement token caching that respects Zoho's token caps
Add credit and concurrency budgeting with backoff
humanMustDo: Sign in to the Zoho API Console and register the Server-based client
Enable Multi-DC and pick the allowed data centers
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into your secrets store
Test with real accounts in several data centers

blockers.symptom: {"error":"invalid_client"} or invalid_code when exchanging a code for a non-US user
blockers.cause: The token request went to accounts.zoho.com instead of the user's accounts-server, or Multi-DC isn't enabled for that DC.
blockers.fix: Use the accounts-server value from the callback for token and refresh calls, and enable Multi-DC for that region.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: We observed invalid_client from accounts.zoho.com with bogus credentials; mapping it to wrong-DC calls is our inference.

blockers.symptom: No refresh_token in the token response
blockers.cause: access_type wasn't set to offline in the authorization request.

blockers.symptom: An older connection for the same user suddenly stops refreshing
blockers.cause: A user can hold at most 20 refresh tokens; generating a 21st invalidates the oldest.
blockers.fix: Don't re-run consent needlessly; reuse the stored refresh token per user.

blockers.cause: More than 10 access tokens requested from one refresh token within 10 minutes.
blockers.fix: Cache access tokens for their 1-hour life and share them across workers.

blockers.symptom: API calls rejected for the rest of the day, or concurrency errors under load
blockers.cause: The org's 24-hour API credit allowance or per-app concurrency limit is used up.
blockers.fix: Reduce call volume, use bulk/COQL and notifications, and queue requests to respect concurrency.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error code wasn't captured in the pages we read.

blockers.cause: redirect_uri doesn't match the one registered in the API Console.
blockers.fix: Register the exact redirect URI and send it identically in both requests.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens don't expire until revoked. Grant codes last 3 minutes, and only 10 grant tokens per client ID can be issued in 10 minutes.

Zoho's live server-info endpoint lists more data centers than the CRM multi-DC docs: it also returns UK, SA, AE, SG and an IN enterprise host (accounts.zohohq.in). Don't hard-code the docs' list of seven.
A refresh token is tied to the organization the user chose at consent and can't be used for another org.

Daily API credits are per org: Free 5,000; Standard 50,000 + 250/user (max 100,000); Professional 50,000 + 500/user; Enterprise 50,000 + 1,000/user; Ultimate 50,000 + 2,000/user. Your app shares them with every other integration in that org.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: 'Shares them with every other integration' is our reading of the per-org allowance.

nuances.text: Zoho's OIDC discovery advertises device-code and jwt-bearer grants plus token introspection and revocation endpoints.
